data.body:
Investigation complete. Root cause: the bursts are EXPECTED negative-access probes
from the private-audit runner, not an external caller and not a missing permission.
The alarm is mis-scoped, not the access control.

## Evidence

Alarm `lmn-staging-private-context-denied` watches raw `AWS/S3 4xxErrors` with
`BucketName=lmn-staging-private-context-896586841071`,
`FilterId=all-private-context-requests`, threshold `Sum > 5` over 300s.

In the 2026-09-18T01:35Z-04:59Z window the S3 access logs hold 96 `403 AccessDenied`
records: `REST.GET.OBJECT` 58, `REST.GET.BUCKET` 24, `REST.PUT.OBJECT` 12,
`REST.HEAD.BUCKET` 2. Every failing principal is an assumed role with a session name
matching `lmn-staging-private-audit-*`.

Representative denial:

```
ts        2026-09-18T02:57:30+00:00
requester arn:aws:sts::896586841071:assumed-role/lmn-staging-api/lmn-staging-private-audit-52d0cc282c73448b-api
operation REST.GET.OBJECT
key       policy/colorado.json
status    403  error_code AccessDenied
agent     aws-sdk-js/3.895.0 exec-env/AWS_Lambda_nodejs20.x
```

The same bucket served `200` in the same minute to
`lmn-staging-private-context-curator/lmn-context-admission` and to
`lmn-staging-report-generator/...-generator` on its allowed prefixes. The
differentiator is policy, not network or KMS.

## Hypotheses tested

1. CONFIRMED - explicit bucket-policy deny for non-approved roles. IAM simulation for
   `lmn-staging-api` returned `explicitDeny` sourced from `ResourcePolicy`; the failing
   sessions are roles excluded by `OnlyCuratorAndGeneratorDataAccess` and
   `OnlyApprovedPrincipalsCanInspectInventory`.
2. REFUTED - KMS key policy. Encryption uses AWS-managed `alias/aws/s3`, whose policy
   admits account principals already authorized by S3. Denials include `ListBucket`,
   where KMS is not consulted.
3. REFUTED - VPC endpoint policy. `describe-vpc-endpoints` for S3 returns `[]`, the
   relevant Lambdas have `VpcConfig: null`, and both working and failing requests used
   public S3 endpoints.

## Status

Bursts have STOPPED. Denial timestamps cluster at 01:39Z (1), 02:51Z (1), 02:57Z (33),
02:58Z (16), 04:45Z (45). Last `403 AccessDenied` was 2026-09-18T04:45:42Z. The last
nonzero alarm datapoint was 2026-09-17T21:55:00-07:00 with value 1; nothing nonzero
through 2026-09-20T09:00Z.

CloudTrail recorded a Terraform `PutBucketPolicy` by `user/joe_frontier` at
2026-09-18T02:57:00Z, immediately before the first large burst - the audit run follows
a policy deploy.

## Recommended remediation - NOT applied

Leave IAM, bucket policy, VPC and KMS unchanged; they enforce the private-context
isolation correctly. Do NOT add the failing app roles to the bucket-policy allowlist,
which would remove that isolation.

Rescope the alarm to count only UNEXPECTED denials:

```
bucket      = lmn-staging-private-context-896586841071
http_status = 403
error_code  = AccessDenied
requester NOT LIKE arn:aws:sts::896586841071:assumed-role/*/lmn-staging-private-audit-*
requester  != arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier
threshold: Sum > 5 over 300 seconds
```

Until that metric exists, pace the audit runner to at most 5 `AccessDenied` responses
per 300s, or run it under explicit alarm suppression.

Note: the account has no CloudTrail trails and no event data stores
(`describe-trails` and `list-event-data-stores` both empty), so S3 data-event denials
are only visible through S3 server access logs.
